uses.label: Bulgarian Greek Catholic Church
uses.finding: The intended Bulgarian audience of the Roman Vulgata books is stated by the 2021 study. A 1985 celebrant book, a 2005 composite and a 2007 seasonal collection are labelled from official lists and primary contents photographs.
uses.limit: No Bulgarian receipt of the 1940/1942/1953 Vulgata books is evidenced; the 1985 book's source and approval leaves and the contents of the 2005 and 2007 books are unseen.
next_sources: Title and approval leaves of Eldarov's 1985 Služebnik (library copy, e.g. the National Library of Bulgaria)
Exarchate archives for earlier Slavonic celebrant copies
Contents of the 2007 Holy Week collection
uses.review_remaining_gap: No Bulgarian receipt of the 1940/1942/1953 Vulgata books; Eldarov 1985 title, approval and source leaves; contents of 2005 and 2007 books; earlier Slavonic celebrant copies in the Sofia Exarchate. A later Vulgata-recension edition (Parenti, ed., Divina liturgia … rito bizantino-slavo di recensione volgata, Rome 2016, cited by Bogataj 2022 p. 263) is a byzantine_slavic lead with no Bulgarian reception evidence.

uses.label: Macedonian Greek Catholic Church

uses.review_remaining_gap: Source-language edition, Macedonian imprint and effective date. Not examined: the period before 2001, when secondary accounts say Macedonian Byzantine Catholics were under the Križevci eparchy (so Križevci-era books and acts are a search route), and the interwar Gevgelija mission (Bogataj 2022 p. 262 mentions Aljančič at Ruski Krstur and Gevgelija 1928–1933).

uses.label: Croatian faithful of the Križevci eparchy
uses.finding: The 2018 Chrysostom book explicitly derives from the Rome 1970 Ruthenian Slavonic printing; the 2017 approval and the five-year 2018 authorization are verified on page images 4 and 5. Earlier Croatian derivatives (1961, 1999, 2005, 2009, 2020) are labelled as deferred translations.
uses.limit: The 1970 original, earlier Croatian Slavonic celebrant books and any post-2023 renewal are not established.
next_sources: A copy of the Rome 1970 Ruthenian Chrysostom printing
Križevci eparchial gazette for the renewal of decree 5/2018
uses.review_remaining_gap: Renewal after the five-year term (early 2023); the 1970 source book itself; Croatian Slavonic celebrant books before 1961; Basil and Presanctified imprints. Corrections: kurecic1999 title and source, kekic2009 content claim, ruthenian1970 related candidates.

uses.label: Slovenian faithful of the Križevci eparchy
uses.finding: A 1933–1965–2022 translation chain; the 2022 translation is from the 1942 Ruthenian Liturgikon, with an original local proskomedia adaptation, and was issued in three role editions presented on 25 May 2023.
uses.limit: Original approval letters and complete printed volumes not acquired.
next_sources: KUD Logos and Križevci eparchy catalogue entries for the three 2023 editions (COBISS.SI)
uses.review_remaining_gap: Approval letters 92/2022, 152/2022 and 14/2023; the printed volumes; which volume carries ISBN 978-961-7155-17-4. Corrections supply the 1933 title and its Latin-diocesan nihil obstat/imprimatur, the 1965 imprimatur and the advance-cited 2022 title.

uses.label: Serbian Rusyn Greek Catholics (Ruski Krstur)
uses.finding: Historical Mukacheve heritage is attested by a specialist catalogue; this is kept separate from the Serbian intended audience of the Vulgata books and from Croatian evidence.
uses.limit: Exact celebrant copies, local reception acts and the print sequence are not located.
next_sources: Ruski Krstur eparchial archive and publication list
Serbian COBISS and Vojvodina library catalogues for Rusyn and Church Slavonic Liturgikons
uses.review_remaining_gap: Exact celebrant copies, local acts and sequence. Not examined: the Križevci-era period (secondary sources say Bačka Rusyn parishes belonged to Križevci until the 2003 exarchate), so pre-2003 Križevci books and acts are a search route; the 2018 Croatian decree postdates the separation and correctly is not extended to Serbia.
